title: Anti-Inflammatory Effects of Camboginol and Cranberry Extract Combination Through the Suppression of Pro-Inflammatory Cytokine Secretion in LPS-Induced RAW 264.7 Macrophages
content: Chronic wounds are often associated with prolonged inflammation and bacterial infection, which can delay tissue repair. Cranberry (Vaccinium macrocarpon) is rich in polyphenolic compounds with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, whereas camboginol, or garcinol, a polyisoprenylated benzophenone derived from Garcinia species, has demonstrated potential anti-inflammatory activity. This study aims to investigate the anti-inflammatory effects of camboginol and cranberry extract, in combination, using lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages, including antibacterial activities. The results demonstrated that both camboginol and cranberry extract exhibited anti-inflammatory effects. Camboginol inhibited TNF-α and IL-6 more than cranberry extract, whereas their combination (C3; 25 µM camboginol and 250 µg/mL cranberry extract) produced the greatest reductions in ROS, NO, and pro-inflammatory cytokines. C3 also showed pronounced suppression of iNOS, COX-2, MMP-9, and MAPK-associated phosphorylation. Furthermore, camboginol and cranberry reduced LPS-induced IKK and NF-κB p65 phosphorylation, with the combination exhibiting the strongest inhibitory effect. Regarding antibacterial activity, camboginol exhibited inhibitory effects against Staphylococcus aureus at both tested concentrations and against Bacillus subtilis and Pseudomonas aeruginosa at the higher concentration. However, cranberry extract showed no detectable antibacterial activity and did not enhance camboginol’s antibacterial effects. In conclusion, camboginol and cranberry extract, particularly their combination, demonstrated promising anti-inflammatory activity, while camboginol contributed to the observed antibacterial effects. These findings support further investigation of their potential incorporation into hydrogel wound dressings.
